title: ‘Hacks’ Stars Hannah Einbinder and Paul W. Downs on the Legacy of ‘Hacks’ and Which Character Needs a Spinoff First
full_text: Aug 1, 2026 11:58pm PT ‘Hacks’ Stars Hannah Einbinder and Paul W. Downs on the Legacy of ‘Hacks’ and Which Character Needs a Spinoff First Awards Circuit Podcast: Also on this episode, Variety TV critic Aramide Tinubu shares her summer TV picks and Emmy nomination hot takes. By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Variety Editor at Large franklinavenue Latest ‘Hacks’ Stars Hannah Einbinder and Paul W. Downs on the Legacy of ‘Hacks’ and Which Character Needs a Spinoff First 4 hours ago John Oliver Extends His HBO Contract to Continue ‘Last Week Tonight’ Through 2027 2 days ago ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Producers on Episode 2’s Surprise Kaley Cuoco Cameo as an Alternate Penny 2 days ago See All Getty Images for HBO Max Hannah Einbinder says working with Gillian Anderson on the new film “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” has actually given her a new perspective on the end of “ Hacks ” and its legacy. “Doing all this press with Gillian for the movie, she talks about ‘X-Files’ constantly,” Einbinder tells Variety ‘s Awards Circuit Podcast . “She’s asked about it constantly. It’s made me feel like, ‘oh, I’m gonna talk about “Hacks” for the rest of my life!’ I’m so happy that will always be something that I can come back to and meditate on and express gratitude for. When you are a part of something that has a deeply connected base of people who love it, that stays.” Related Stories Why I'm Suing to Block the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger (Guest Column) Court Hears Argument on States' Move to Pause Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Meanwhile, given how many photo shoots and events Paul W. Downs and his “Hacks” co-star Megan Stalter seem to show up at, why isn’t there a Jimmy and Kayla spinoff in the works? Popular on Variety “I would love for it to happen, and I have said this: You know we had a very specific plan for the way we wanted to end the story in the finale,” he says. “It’s such it’s so much pressure to deliver a satisfying ending … so, even to the last minute, even though we had this plan for a long time, we were like, ‘Should we stretch it out? Should we do two half seasons?’ But in the end, I’m so happy we stuck to our guns, and it resonated with people the way that it did. And because of that, I don’t I don’t want anything else to come after. I want that to be the last thing people remember.” When grilled about “Jimmy and Kayla,” he adds, “getting to play these characters and having these characters evolve as much as they have over the five seasons has been so gratifying that it’s terrifying to think there won’t be more between the two of us. But I think it would have to be something different.” OK … we’re getting somewhere. So what might a “Hacks” spinoff look like? “There’s so many characters in the show that if we could do a universe, I want to see Mayor Jo in her first election. I want to see Marty coming to to Vegas in the ’70s.” Einbinder likes the Mayor Jo idea. “‘Better Call Saul’ vibes,” she says. “Her just being a fucking absolute criminal. Are you kidding? I’m in the freaking seats with the popcorn on that one.” Give it time. Maybe we’ll wear them down! But for now, we’ve got Downs and Einbinder on this week’s Awards Circuit Podcast, where they talk more about the “Hacks” ending and what they’ve got in store next. Plus, they take the 10 Questions quiz! But first, on the Roundtable, Variety TV critic Aramide Tinubu joins us to give some of her summer TV picks and hot takes on the Emmy noms. Listen below! He might be a bit biased, but Downs raves about Einbinder’s part in the upcoming slasher film “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” which opens August 7. “I’ll give you the review,” he says. “This is a pull quote now from Variety . Absolutely beautiful, absolutely terrifying and absolutely funny. And Hannah is a revelation. She is such a star. I’m not even kidding. The stuff that she does, her range being on display yet again in this is really impressive.” As for Downs, Lucia Aniello and Jen Statsky, the trio has a number of projects in the works — including one in development with Kaley Cuoco — although she’s busy on something else right now, so schedules will have to align for their project. And then the trio also has another project they’re working on for HBO. “I can say it’s a it’s a limited series,” he says. “It’s an hourlong limited. I can say that. So it’s a slight tone shift, but there’s definitely going to be humor.” Einbinder says she’d be game to join them again for this next project. “I told Paul, Jen and Lucia that I want to be their non-problematic Rob Schneider. I just want to pop up in everything they do forever.” Meanwhile, Einbinder says she’s still thinking a lot about her time on “Hacks,” and how she found a video that she recorded for herself in Season 1. Now it feels like a bit of a time capsule: “It was in my trailer, and the sound is pretty muffled, and it’s kind of a shitty video, but I just was kind of reflecting, like kind of a diary, and one of the things that I said was ‘I think these people are going to mean so much to me.’” Einbinder’s come a long way in those six years since “Hacks” first became a reality. “Most nights when I get into bed and feel the relief of making it back to my bed at the end of a long day, I go, ‘wow.’ I just am filled with gratitude. This experience has made so much possible for me in every conceivable way. On an emotional level, obviously we have a very strong bond. When I was auditioning for Ava initially, I was opening for other comics on the road. That went away because of COVID, and the job I had before that was working at a coffee shop, and that also went away. I was just really, ‘I actually don’t know what I’m gonna do.’ And so just on every level, [this success] has never been lost on me.” 10 QUESTIONS WITH HANNAH EINBINDER and PAUL W. DOWNS: 1. Childhood nickname: Einbinder: “‘Pud,’ short for ‘Pudding.’ My parents called me that.” Downs: “‘Chubb.’ I think it came from my love of pasta and pizza. I think it honestly came from my love of Swiss Miss. I would take Swiss Miss packets with half and half, and I would make like a sludge that I would drink. It was my version of child cocaine, I guess.” 2. Something you loved as a kid but can’t believe you were into it now: Downs: “I used to kind of collect these, they were basically little figurines that were like a dragon or an Excalibur or a wizard, and they were on amethyst. They were sold at a kiosk at the Rockaway Town Square Mall, and I was into these bizarre — I don’t know what that is. Fantasy figurines. They were also very like Sedona. You know, they were very like hippie figurines. I can’t believe I was so into that” Einbinder: “I have done so much inner child work that I have love and affection for the things that I maybe was into. I took baton. I had a baton unit. I was very into baton at one time. I did baton classes. I learned from a stripper named Heather. Thank you, Heather. She taught baton on the side. She was like, ‘I do flaming baton at my where I dance,’ and we were like, ‘We want to come see you dance, Heather!’ And she was like, ‘It’s not for kids.’” 3. Go-to Karaoke or sing-in-the-shower song: Einbinder: “‘What’s Up,’ by 4 Non Blondes.” Downs: “‘All I Wanna Do’ by Sheryl Crow. It’s a real crowd pleaser.” 4. Give me an alternate title for your show: [Not asked] 5. What’s your secret talent? : Downs: “I can give a good massage.” Einbinder: “I can create a bubble ring underwater. Or a smoke ring. I can do that too. But that’s featured in the show ‘Hacks.’” 6. Favorite ice cream flavor : Downs: “As a kid, I loved strawberry. Now I want like a like a dark chocolate double fudge chunk.” Einbinder: “Mint chip.” 7. The one item you couldn’t live without : Einbinder: “Cell phone.” Downs: “I was gonna say toothpaste. You really want toothpaste.” 8. What TV show in all of history do you wish you were a cast member of? : Einbinder: “‘Sopranos,’ ‘Mad Men.’” Downs: “Some of my favorite shows like ‘Arrested Development’ or ‘Succession’ or ‘Fleabag,’ I don’t know that I want to be on those shows. I think I want to be on ‘Friends.’ I think I would have had a blast.” 9. Fictional character you most admire : [Not asked] 10. Your favorite piece of advice : Einbinder: “‘Faster and funnier.’” Downs: “I’ve uttered those words. You know what else I uttered recently, and I’m taking a great piece of advice that Maya Angelou gave to Oprah, which is when someone tells you who they are, believe them the first time. I think that’s a really good piece of advice.” Variety’s “Awards Circuit” podcast, hosted by Clayton Davis, Jazz Tangcay, Emily Longeretta and Michael Schneider, who also produces, is your one-stop source for lively conversations about the best in film and television. Each episode, “Awards Circuit” features interviews with top film and TV talent and creatives, discussions and debates about awards races and industry headlines, and much more. title: Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock Surprise Fans at ‘Practical Magic’ Screening in Hollywood Forever Cemetery for L.A.’s Cinespia
full_text: Aug 1, 2026 9:30pm PT Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock Surprise Fans at ‘Practical Magic’ Screening in Hollywood Forever Cemetery for L.A.’s Cinespia 'Practical Magic 2' stars Joey King and Maisie Williams led a 'Midnight Margaritas' toast By Angelique Jackson Plus Icon Angelique Jackson angelique814 Latest Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock Surprise Fans at ‘Practical Magic’ Screening in Hollywood Forever Cemetery for L.A.’s Cinespia 6 hours ago ‘Barbie’ Sequel Stalls as David Zaslav Won’t Approve Bigger Salaries for Ryan Gosling and Margot Robbie 18 hours ago Jon Bernthal on His ‘Brotherly Dynamic’ With Tom Holland in ‘Spider-Man’ and ‘The Odyssey,’ and Why Punisher Is Peter Parker’s ‘Cautionary Tale’ 2 days ago See All Getty Images for CinemaCon Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman made a surprise appearance at a screening of “ Practical Magic ” on Saturday night in L.A. Attendees came to the place, the Hollywood Forever Cemetery, for magic — and many, many Midnight Margaritas — but few expected an appearance by the Owens sisters themselves to introduce the 1998 cult classic. “Thank you so much for coming out tonight. Perfect movie to show in a cemetery,” Bullock, who stars as Sally Owens, said over the crowd’s roar of enthusiasm. “We should also thank the spirits that are floating around us as well because you’re on their seats.” Related Stories AMC Theatres Chief Adam Aron Pushes for Paramount Warner Bros. Merger, Says 'Thanks, but No Thanks' to State AG’s Blocking Deal Paramount Skydance Agrees to Link Merger Antitrust Case to Pre-Existing Paramount+ Subscriber Suit Kidman, who plays Gilly, added: “Thank you for all your support for getting this 2nd film made that’s coming to you.” Popular on Variety Then, Bullock introduced the “next generation” of Owens sisters: Joey King and Maisie Williams, who play Sally’s adult daughters in Warner Bros.’ sure-to-be-spellbinding sequel, in theaters Sept. 11. The duo sauntered on the screen with margaritas in hand. “To the coven,” Kidman said, proposing that the crowd — clad in all types of 90s witchy attire, from flowy black robes and pointy hats “Practical Magic” t-shirts — raise their glasses. “Maisie and I are so excited to be joining the coven as Kylie and Antonia,” King told the crowd. “We really hope you enjoy the new movie as much as we did making it.” View this post on Instagram “Practical Magic 2,” directed by Susanne Bier, “returns to a world steeped in moonlit mischief and powerful ancestral magic, as the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all in a must-see cinematic event of fun, magic and mayhem.” The new movie follows 28 years later, as Sally bakes cakes and avoids men, while Gilly attracts men named Chad on Tinder. But the Owens family’s 300-year-old curse carries one generation forward, striking Sally daughter Kylie’s and her lover (Xolo Maridueña), who gets hit by a car while bicycling with several bouquets of roses. Kylie is determined to reverse the curse by any means necessary, forcing Sally and Gillian to band together to keep her away from the darkness and break the spell for good. Lee Pace also stars in the film, with Stockard Channing and Dianne Wiest returning and Frances and Jet Owens, Sally and Gilly’s aunts. Akiva Goldsman and Georgia Pritchett wrote the script for the sequel, which is based on the 2021 novel “The Book of Magic” by Alice Hoffman, the fourth in her “Practical Magic” book series. Denise DiNovi, Bullock and Kidman produced the Warner Bros. film. Andrew Kosove, Broderick Johnson, Donald Sabourin and Hoffman serve as executive producers. The special “Practical Magic” screening was part of Cinespia ‘s annual lineup of exhibitions at the Hollywood Forever Cemetery. The outdoor screening series, which is celebrating its 25th anniversary, has “The Mummy,” a double feature of Mia Goth’s “X” and “Pearl,” “Coming to America” and a 40th anniversary showing of “Labyrinth” scheduled for the month of August. Cinespia is presented by Amazon MGM Studios and Prime Video. title: Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman Make Surprise Appearance at ‘Practical Magic’ Screening
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 9:01pm Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman promote "Practical Magic 2" during CinemaCon on April 14 in Las Vegas. Ethan Miller/Getty Images Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman are getting an early start on spooky season. The duo made a surprise appearance at a Cinespia screening of their beloved 1998 movie Practical Magic on Saturday night, arriving to screams from the crowd at Hollywood Forever Cemetery. “[ Practical Magic ] is [the] perfect movie to show at a cemetery,” Bullock said to the crowd, as Kidman added, “Thank you for all your support for getting this second film made that’s coming to you very soon.” They also introduced the sequel’s new additions in Joey King and Maisie Williams, sharing a toast among themselves and the audience. Related Stories TV Taylor Sheridan Returning for an On-Camera Role in 'Lioness' Season 3 TV A 10-Year-Old Budding "Hollywood Reporter" Gets Her First Red Carpet Experience, Interviewing the Stars of 'L.O.L. Surprise! The Next Headliner' The night helped stir up excitement ahead of the upcoming sequel , which sees Bullock and Kidman reprising their roles as orphaned sisters Sally and Gillian Owens. In the original, the two — raised by their witch aunts Aunt Jet (Dianne Wiest) and Aunt Franny (Stockard Channing) — embrace witchcraft after avoiding it most of their lives. The sisters work to learn how to use their powers to ward off a curse that threatens women in the family from finding love, and leaves men they fall in love with dead. Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman make a special appearance at a @cinespia screening of #PracticalMagic , alongside their sequel costars Joey King and Maisie Williams pic.twitter.com/kc3kRD0xNZ — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) August 2, 2026 In Practical Magic 2 , set 25 years later, Bullock’s character now has two daughters — played by King and Williams — who have their own witchy abilities. King’s character discovers dark family secrets that plunge the Owens family into a crisis, and the women must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel them once and for all. Wiest and Channing have also returned for the follow-up, alongside other new additions Lee Pace, Xolo Maridueña and Solly McLeod. The Perfect Couple ‘s Susanne Bier directed the film, which hits theaters Sept. 11. Bullock and Kidman are producing the sequel alongside Denise Di Novi, who was also behind the 1998 movie. Practical Magic is also returning to theaters for one night only, on Aug. 11, in preparation for the new film. THR

Following the actor’s death at age 80 , his co-stars from the acclaimed HBO series paid tribute to the man who was known for his portrayal of Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero during the show’s six-season run from 1999 to 2007. Jamie-Lynn Sigler, who played Meadow Soprano, wrote, “A wonderful actor, a kind and loving man. It was an honor to know you and work with you.” Related Stories News Vincent Pastore Dies: ‘The Sopranos’ Star Was 80 Obituaries Charley Scalies Dies: ‘The Wire’ & ‘The Sopranos’ Actor Was 84 Michael Imperioli, who played Christopher Moltisanti, wrote on Instagram , “Our beloved friend and collaborator VINCENT PASTORE has passed away. Vinny was a kind-hearted brother who cared deeply about his family and friends. I will miss him always.” Watch on Deadline Lorraine Bracco, who played Dr. Jennifer Melfi, wrote, “Such a funny & charming man… just a beautiful soul. Travel well Vincenzo. pic.twitter.com/sybh6LOWvm — 🇺🇸🇮🇱🇺🇦🕉Stevie Van Zandt☮️💙 (@StevieVanZandt) August 2, 2026 Joe Pantoliano, who played Ralph Cifaretto, wrote , “God bless him. He made it to 80. title: Scott Hylands Dead: ‘Night Heat’ & ‘Fargo’ Actor Was 83
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Vincent Pastore Tributes: ‘The Sopranos’ Alums Jamie-Lynn Sigler, Michael Imperioli & More Remember “Kind-Hearted Brother” Scott Hylands Dead: ‘Night Heat’ & ‘Fargo’ Actor Was 83 CBS News Correspondent Nikki Battiste Joins NBC’s ‘Early Today’ As Anchor: “A True Homecoming” View All August 1, 2026 5:01pm Scott Hylands in 'Night Heat' (1985-89) Alliance Entertainment/Courtesy Everett Collection Scott Hylands , the actor known for playing Detective Kevin “OB” O’Brien in Night Heat , has died. He was 83. The Canadian actor died on Wednesday, July 29, his cinematographer son Luke Hylands announced in a statement memorializing his “forever hero and best friend” on social media. “Husband, Father, Actor, Director, Writer, Storyteller, Friend, and lover of life,” he wrote on Instagram . “I am heartbroken to share the news that my Dad Scott has passed away Wednesday night. Myself and my family are still trying to process this horrible loss.” Related Stories Documentary 'A Life Illuminated': Of Bioluminescence, Mysterious Sea Creatures, And A Woman Scientist's Groundbreaking Quest News CBS News Correspondent Nikki Battiste Joins NBC's 'Early Today' As Anchor: "A True Homecoming" Luke continued, “There simply are not enough words I can say about you right now. You are my forever hero and my best friend. Always and forever. I love you. Goodbye Dad. xo” Watch on Deadline Born Feb. 27, 1943 in Lethbridge, Alberta, Canada, Scott Hylands Douglas was raised in British Columbia, where he studied zoology at University of British Columbia before transferring to theater arts. After college, he pursued acting in New York City, where he made his off-Broadway debut as the lead in a 1965 production of Billy Liar . He also performed with the American Conservatory Theater in San Francisco for several years before his onscreen debut in Daddy’s Gone A-Hunting (1969). View this post on Instagram He went on to appear in films like Operation Snafu (1970), Fools (1970), Slipstream (1973), Earthquake (1974), Bittersweet Love (1976) and The Boys in Company “C” (1978), as well as shows like Griff , Kung Fu , The Magician , Wonder Woman , Police Story , The Waltons and Hart to Hart . Upon returning to Canada in the ’80s, Hylands landed the role of Detective Kevin “OB” O’Brien in the the CTV/CBS police crime drama Night Heat from 1985 to ’89. The actor was also known for playing Father Travis in ABC’s V (2009-2011). Over the years, Hylands also appeared on shows like NYPD Blue , The Outer Limits , The X-Files , Stargate SG-1 , Supernatural , Fargo , Heartland and Wynonna Earp , as well as films like Rememory (2017) and Elsewhere (2019). Scott Hylands is survived by wife Veronica, son Luke and daughter Rebecca. The Hollywood Reporter was first to break the news of Hylands’ death. title: ‘Wonder Man’ Star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Reacts to Marvel Series Cancellation: “See You at the Emmys”

The streamer picked up the series for a second season in March before reversing course and canceling the renewal on Thursday. The decision came as a surprise after Wonder Man had a solid debut on Disney+ in late January, drawing 618 million minutes of viewing time during its premiere week, according to Nielsen’s streaming ratings. title: Gavin Newsom Reportedly Concerned About State Antitrust Suit Against Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 1, 2026 4:46pm California Gov. Gavin Newsom Heather Diehl/Getty Images Governor Gavin Newsom is concerned about the antitrust lawsuit filed by 12 state attorneys general led by California against Paramount ‘s $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, and what it will mean for the entertainment industry, according to The Wall Street Journal . In a Friday report, sources told the WSJ that Newsom has said if the merger is blocked due to the lawsuit, state employment will suffer. The outlet also notes that “Newsom’s office has encouraged Attorney General Rob Bonta’s office, which has independent authority to file such suits, to find a resolution out of court.” Related Stories Movies 'Barbie' Sequel Stalled as Warner Bros. Tries to Reach Deals With Greta Gerwig, Margot Robbie, Ryan Gosling TV Taylor Sheridan Returning for an On-Camera Role in 'Lioness' Season 3 Reps for Newsom and Bonta declined the WSJ ‘s requests for comment; The Hollywood Reporter also reached out to California’s governor for comment. On July 13, the states filed a lawsuit alleging that the merger would combine two of Hollywood’s top five studios, which would lead to higher prices, less movies in theaters and a decrease in the variety and quality of content. “There is no debate here: This merger will snuff out competition, drive up prices, diminish content quality, and produce fewer movies and shows each year,” said California Attorney General Rob Bonta at a press conference at the time. The filing of the suit led to a temporary pause on the merger, ruled by U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín on July 20; that temporary restraining order was subsequently extended on July 23. One day later, Paramount agreed to hold off on the acquisition until the court makes a decision of whether or not the deal violates antitrust laws. In a court document filed on July 24, Paramount said they will not consummate the acquisition until June 2027 or five days after the court issues a ruling on the case, whichever is earlier. Alongside California, Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon and Washington are involved in the suit. While organizations including Cinema United have shown support for the suit and actors Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong called on the U.K. to block the Paramount–Warner Bros. merger, Newsom is not the only democratic power player to reportedly push for a settlement. On Monday, Ari Emanuel, WME executive chairman and CEO of TKO, wrote an op-ed for the WSJ in support of Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. “When government officials manipulate markets to reach political outcomes, antitrust stops protecting competition and starts threatening it,” Emanuel wrote. “The attorneys general should drop this case and get back to enforcing the laws as they are written. Let Hollywood creatives get back to trying to rip each other’s heads off at the box office, in streaming, online and everywhere else we compete. It’s what we’re best at.” THR

title: K-pop Girl Group IVE is Ready for Their Next Big Adventure
full_text: × Skip to main content K-pop girl group IVE. Courtesy of Starship Entertainment It’s a Tuesday in early spring, and the young women in IVE are gathered in what appears to be a warehouse turned studio near L.A.’s Arts District for a Vevo Studios shoot. The performers gather around a monitor playing back their most recent take. They watch the screen intently as makeup artists and hair stylists give quick touch ups. Earlier this year, the girl group put out their second studio album, Revive+ . The six-member outfit, comprising members Yujin, Wonyoung, Gaeul, Rei, Liz and Leeseo, kicked off their new era with the pre-release single “Bang Bang,” one of the two songs they’re performing for Vevo. Related Stories Music Sam Fender and Olivia Dean Have the Longest-Running No. 1 in U.K. History Music Grammys CEO "Saddened" Over BTS Decision to Not Submit for Awards There’s little downtime, with the group performing several takes of them singing and dancing live for the cameras, but the members of IVE find a few moments of rest. In those moments, they look less like the global superstars they undoubtedly are, and more like the young women they also are — playing with their phones and chatting amongst each other during their brief breaks. “We’re so enthusiastic,” says Wonyoung about being in Los Angeles. It’s hours later, and we’ve gathered in the basement of Live Nation’s Beverly Hills office. “We really love working in L.A., so we’re really happy.” At just 21 years old, Wonyoung has been an active K-pop idol for eight years, having won popular Korean music competition series Produce 48 at the age of 14 and joining the temporary girl group Iz*One, alongside fellow IVE member and the group’s leader, Yujin. The now-22-year-old was only a year older than her. IVE had plenty going for themselves as group when their first single “Eleven” was released in 2021 — two K-pop veterans with Wonyoung and Yujin, a powerhouse vocalist with the now 21-year-old Liz, a skilled rapper and songwriter with now 23-year-old Gaeul, a charismatic and charming rapper with the now 22-year-old Rei and an adorable singer and youngest member with the now 19-year-old Leeseo. It should come as no the surprise the group was a near-instant success. The group dominated domestic charts and toured the world, but they’re still getting new experiences, much like this Vevo shoot. “This is the first time that we’ve done anything like this in the U.S.,” Rei says. The rapper, perhaps IVE’s most online member, admits she’s watched other performances from the series online and the studio was smaller than she expected it to be. “We’ve done a lot of performances in Korea and filmed videos of ‘Bang Bang’ a lot,” she continues. “But it was a special performance.” Now, the group is back in the U.S. for their Show What I Am world tour, which lands Saturday (Aug. 1) in L.A. The group will return to the Kia Forum after last performing at the arena in 2024. The group comes back with new performances, including solo stages from each member — a continuation of the group’s decision to each have a solo song on Revive+ . Below, IVE speaks with The Hollywood Reporter about their latest music, touring, the realities of being a K-pop idol and what they’ve learned from one another. Can you tell me about your most recent single “Bang Bang? ” GAEUL “Bang Bang” symbolizes a new start for us, just like the title of our album, Revive+ . Do you feel a pressure to try new things ever? WONYOUNG More than a pressure, we really feel excited and like [there’s] a happy virus thing inside of us. [It’s] really less [about pressure] and more that [these] six girls can do it. Rei, Gaeul, Jang Wonyoung, An Yujin, Leeseo and Liz of IVE attend the media showcase for IVE’s second full-length album ‘Revive+’ on February 23, 2026 at YES24 Live Hall in Gwangjin-gu, Seoul, South Korea. HLL/Imazins via Getty Images You’ve been together for a while now. Do you feel anything has shifted for you as performers or as people? Does being an idol get any easier for you as time goes on? LIZ Inwardly, I don’t feel much different from when I was a student. I think because we did have to start working earlier on, we were able to reflect on that and learn new things. Leeseo, I’m particularly interested in hearing your experience with this. A lot of people your age are just starting to think about what the rest of their life looks like. You’ve already had a career for quite a long time now. How are you feeling about where you’re at right now? LEESEO Sometimes I do want to live a normal life like other people my age, but I feel like with the five members I have, this team, is just so fun. I’m really glad that I’m in IVE. I’m really satisfied with the music and the vibe of our group, so I’m really excited for the future. Your music has definitely evolved alongside you. Do you ever feel any anxiety or any excitement about trying new things? Do you have worries about losing the spark of what makes your music work for you if you try these new things? YUJIN Especially with “Bang Bang,” I was kind of worried because it really was a new genre that we haven’t tried before. But it got so much more attention and love than we thought [it would], so I think it’s worth it. We try hard to make our performances better and better, so I feel proud. Success tends to come with more eyes on you, whether that be fans or the general public. You’re young women — a lot of people are given more grace be young and do things, but everything you do is often looked at pretty critically. Do you ever feel misundersood? Do you ever wish people could see you differently? LIZ Something that I would want to do if there wasn’t so much pressure is freely travel and go about my everyday life. But with all the love that we receive, there’s risks that inevitably come with it, so I think it’s something that we have to accept. Many people can think what they want and they have their own impression of what IVE is. But if you end up caring about all of those opinions, then you can’t live your own life. We try not to care too much about what these other people think and just keep going. GAEUL There’s a lot of misunderstandings and some things can not be in our favor, but we still try our best in our own way. We believe that if we just keep doing what we want to do, then we’ll be able to go our own way. IVE members Rei, Gaeul, Jang Wonyoung, An Yujin, Leeseo and Liz. The Chosunilbo JNS/Imazins via Getty Images) Is there anything about how you all are together that would surprise people? WONYOUNG Maybe audiences see us on stage or during performance and [think] we’re [just] professional. But we’re just six girls or high school girlies, so that’s a fun part [of us people don’t get to see]. All versions of IVE might be a surprise, in a good way, because we’re just girls. You’re getting ready to go back out on tour. What does preparation look like? YUJIN I have such a good memories from our last tour. I really had fun, so I’m looking forward to it. I’m preparing a lot of medicine, so I don’t get a cold. Is there something your teammates have made you better at over the years? REI When we practice, we definitely give advice to help each other. For me, personally, during our debut there were a lot of things I didn’t know. Especially just Korean language-wise, so the members have really helped me. I’m the only foreign member, so sometimes it was a little bit lonely for me. But the members really took care of me. That really warmed my heart as the years went on. Last year, when KPop Demon Hunters was really popular, you posted a video of you doing the “I Am” choreography to “Golden.” That was very cute, why did you decide to do that? WONYOUNG We felt like there was a little coincidence between that song and our song, “I Am.” We felt like we could relate to that song, so we just made a cute video of our choreography and the Demon Hunters song. It was a good thing because people loved that set. When you’re preparing for a comeback or a tour, what’s the most important thing for you all? WONYOUNG Our health. Our health is the most important thing always, so we just try to get a lot of sleep and a lot of food. THR

title: ‘A Life Illuminated’: Of Bioluminescence, Mysterious Sea Creatures, And A Woman Scientist’s Groundbreaking Quest
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Emmy Contender Judd Apatow On “Piss-Your-Pants” Funny Mel Brooks, His Nikki Glaser Collab, And That Seth Rogen-Anne Hathaway ‘Knocked Up’ Story Chris Hemsworth’s Wild State Boards ‘Learning To Fly’, Ultra Marathon-Themed Documentary From Award-Winning Director Max Lowe Doc Talk Podcast: Director Sara Dosa On Her Oscar Contender ‘Time And Water’, Elegy For Iceland’s Disappearing Ice View All August 1, 2026 4:33pm Dr. Edie Widder (right) below the ocean surface in 'A Life Illuminated' Sandbox Films Director Tasha Van Zandt went to great lengths to make her documentary A Life Illuminated – and to enormous depths. More than 3,000 feet, in fact. Van Zandt descended over half a mile to the ocean floor in a submersible to film the work of pioneering marine biologist Dr. Edie Widder , who has observed and studied more deep ocean phenomena than perhaps anyone alive. Her discoveries have “transformed how we perceive life in the deep sea,” the filmmaker writes. “[Widder] began her career at a time when the deep sea was considered a dark, empty void. But Edie dared to look diﬀerently. Through her courage, curiosity, and her lens, she revealed the ocean as a glowing, dynamic world.” Related Stories Documentary ‘A Life Illuminated’ Clip: Take Plunge With Undersea Explorer Edie Widder In TIFF World Premiere Documentary Documentary Sandbox Films, XTR Team On ‘A Life Illuminated,’ Feature Doc On Pioneering Marine Biologist Edie Widder Widder has uncovered a once-hidden “language of light” – dazzling bioluminescence that pervades ocean depths. Watch on Deadline A bioluminescent jellyfish seen in the North Atlantic Ocean. Reinhard Dirscherl/ullstein bild via Getty Images “Edie actually says, ‘Because so much of our ocean world is bioluminescent and the ocean is so vast, bioluminescence may be the most common form of communication on our planet,’” Van Zandt said at a Q&A Wednesday that followed a screening of her film in Santa Monica, CA, a short distance from the Pacific. “’What is this language we don’t understand?’” It took the development of submersibles capable of withstanding tremendous atmospheric pressures to enter that sunken water world. But something more was required to reveal the life forms and their activities so far below the surface – truly innovative thinking that has been the hallmark of Dr. Widder’s scientific career. She led the invention and design of multiple devices to “enable unobtrusive deep-sea observations,” as noted by the Ocean Research & Conservation Association (ORCA), which Widder founded. Dr. Edie Widder earlier in her career. Sandbox Films As the documentary explores, Widder developed an “eye-in-the-sea” system to remotely monitor deep ocean marine life. It uses far-red illumination, which she understood wouldn’t bother creatures in the depths because most of them don’t perceive infrared light. Widder also created an “electronic jellyfish,” an ingenious optical lure aimed to tempt sea creatures into camera range. By deploying one of the lures, she became the first person to capture video of a giant squid alive, a multi-tentacled animal trying to make a dinner of the faux jellyfish. “In 2012, I, along with the rest of the world, saw this first footage of a live giant squid in its natural habitat,” Van Zandt recounted. “And I was transfixed by it, but it wasn’t until years later that I started to really sit with the question of who was the person behind the camera and how did this [footage] come to be? And so, in 2020, I reached out to Edie Widder for the first time. And on our very first conversation, she started to share how that was just one of hundreds of discoveries she had made in this quest to transform how we see our ocean planet. And that is when the spark for this film began.” A submersible deep below the ocean surface in ‘A Life Illuminated’ Sandbox Films Eventually, Van Zandt took the plunge with Dr. Widder. “When I was able to dive with Edie, we saw things that likely no one has ever seen before, even beyond this film that we couldn’t even capture on camera because it was so faint to the human eye. And it was remarkable,” the director said. “There are incredible creatures in our oceans that we can’t even begin to fathom how to even look for yet. So, it was completely life-changing.” For decades now, Widder has been documenting the light show created by marine animals that mix chemicals in their bodies to generate bioluminescence. Van Zandt structures the film around the scientist’s mission to capture the flashback effect (her white whale, as Edie describes it), an attempt to see how bioluminescent creatures respond when they’re flashed with light from an otherwise darkened sub. It was a daunting task for Van Zandt and director of photography-producer Sebastian Zeck to try to reveal that experiment. (L-R) Producer-director Tasha Van Zandt and producer-director of photography Sebastian Zeck at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 7, 2025. Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images for IMDb “Filming in the deep sea in complete darkness from a submersible is a huge technical challenge, but everything sort of came together on that very last dive,” Zeck explained at the Q&A. “We used these specialized cameras provided by Canon to film that [flashback effect] sequence. Light sensitivity in photography is measured in what’s called ISO. Normally in a daylight setting, we’re shooting at ISO 800 or so. The sequence at the end of the film, we shot at ISO 100,000. So, that gives you a sense of the sensitivity required.” The attempt by humans to communicate with marine animals may evoke, for some, a classic Steven Spielberg film about first contact with extraterrestrials. “It really felt like all of the [marine] life was kind of responding in this fantastical way and truly felt like Close Encounters ,” Van Zandt marveled. “We flashed the lights, everything flashed back. And it felt like we were in the center of the Milky Way, but with blue glitter all around us. It was glowing and sparking. And just like the 4th of July — like [Edie] describes from her first experience. But then in the distance, we were seeing things that the camera couldn’t even capture. There was life swooshing and sweeping and this glowing golden, amber-colored creature that we don’t even really know what it was that was off in the distance. And also something fascinating is that the camera picked up this little creature called a tomopterid worm, which glows kind of a golden orange color that flashed along with all of the blue bioluminescence we were seeing.” Sandbox Films A Life Illuminated , from Sandbox Films and XTR, premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival last September, going on to screen at the Camden International Film Festival in Maine, Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival in Arkansas, CPH:DOX in Copenhagen, SFFILM’s Doc Stories and many other festivals in the U.S. and abroad. It began its theatrical run on July 24 at DCTV Firehouse Cinema in Manhattan and the documentary opens Sunday at the Roxie Theater in San Francisco (where Van Zandt and Zeck are based). The 12:50 p.m. Roxie screening on Sunday will be followed by a Q&A moderated by oceanographer Sylvia Earle. With its spectacular imagery of bioluminescent creatures, not to mention a giant squid measuring somewhere between 2-4 storeys tall, this is a film that demands to be seen on the big screen. That’s the closest most of us will ever come to observing the astounding sights Edie Widder has witnessed for decades. Van Zandt says she regards her protagonist as an inspiration. “Going into the [final] dive… one of my greatest fears was how would I respond, if I would feel fearful, if I would panic. And she kept saying to us, ‘Just focus on curiosity instead of fear.’ And when we went down on the dive, that was really the guiding factor. There were definitely moments where I had to say, ‘Curiosity over fear, curiosity over fear,’” Van Zandt recalled. “This lifetime of seeing things no one’s ever seen before and breaking depth limits and just so many courageous moments that she’s lived through has really instilled in her this incredible grounded-ess. It’s really remarkable.” Samara Weaving Lands Emma Frost Role In Disney/Marvel’s Reboot Pic Vincent Pastore Dies, ‘The Sopranos’ Cast Reacts Netflix Mountaineer Nirmal Purja Dies In Avalanche Dermot Mulroney To Leave NBC Drama ‘Chicago Fire’ Early In Season 15 Read More About: Comments

title: Scott Hylands, Star of TV’s ‘Night Heat’ on Both Sides of the Border, Dies at 83
full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 4:24pm Scott Hylands Courtesy Everett Collection Scott Hylands, who starred as the cynical Det. Kevin “O.B.” O’Brien on the 1980s cop show Night Heat , the first Canadian original drama series to simultaneously air in the U.S., has died. He was 83. Hylands died July 29, his son, Luke Hylands, announced . A longtime resident of Salt Spring Island in British Columbia, he was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia in October 2021. The Canadian actor had portrayed his share of villains and heavies in guest spots on U.S. television for about two decades when he returned north to star as a good guy — finally! — in Night Heat , filmed in Toronto. Related Stories TV Vincent Pastore, the Mobster "Big Pussy" on 'The Sopranos,' Dies at 80 Movies Richard L. O'Connor, Emmy-Winning Producer, Dies at 96 On the documentary-style series, conceived by onetime New York City detective Sonny Grosso — who with partner Eddie Egan helped bring down the “French Connection” drug-smuggling ring in the 1960s — Hylands portrayed the veteran cop O’Brien alongside Jeff Wincott as his younger, hot-headed partner, Frank Giambone. Meanwhile, Allan Royal played Tom Kirkwood, who writes about the pair in his “Night Heat” newspaper column (he’s also the series’ narrator). Each episode represented one shift in the show’s unnamed city and was shot between the hours of 6 p.m. and 4 a.m. The series ran for four seasons and 96 episodes, from January 1985 through January 1989, on CTV in Canada and in late night on CBS. (It often out-rated Johnny Carson’s Tonight Show in some markets.) From left: Jeff Wincott, Allan Royal and Scott Hylands in a promotional photo for ‘Night Heat.’ Alliance Entertainment/Courtesy Everett Collection Scott Hylands Douglas was born on Feb. 27, 1943, in Lethbridge, Alberta. His mother, Ruth, was a nurse and a math teacher; his father, Walter, was killed in action in 1945 during World War II. He attended Shawnigan Lake Boys School on Vancouver Island, graduated from the University of British Columbia in 1964 and then headed to New York, where he landed the lead in a 1965 off-Broadway production of Billy Liar . After several years in San Francisco with the American Conservatory Theater, he made his onscreen debut by starring as the deranged ex-boyfriend in Daddy’s Gone a-Hunting (1969), directed by Mark Robson and written by Lorenzo Semple Jr. and Larry Cohen . He spent the 1970s showing up in the films Slipstream (1973), Earthquake (1974) and The Boys in Company C (1978) and on episodes of such series as The Streets of San Francisco , Kung Fu , Harry O , Police Woman , Cannon , Medical Center , Baretta , Wonder Woman and Police Story and in the 1978-79 miniseries Centennial . After Night Heat ended its run, Hylands worked on such shows as NYPD Blue , The X-Files , Due South , Stargate SG-1 , The Outer Limits , V , Once Upon a Time and Wynonna Earp . Perhaps most notably during this stretch, he played Ennis Stuccy, the stepfather of Carrie Coon’s Department of Homeland Security agent Gloria Burgle, on the third season of FX’s Fargo in 2017. In addition to his son, survivors include his wife of 36 years, Veronica, and his daughter, Rebecca. “I was lucky to have worked with him on my first big acting job,” Wincott told the Toronto Sun in 2021. “He taught me a lot. He was always prepared, professional, and he cared deeply about doing good work, a lesson and example I carried with me throughout my career.” THR

title: CBS News Correspondent Nikki Battiste Joins NBC’s ‘Early Today’ As Anchor: “A True Homecoming”
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Vincent Pastore Tributes: ‘The Sopranos’ Alums Jamie-Lynn Sigler, Michael Imperioli & More Remember “Kind-Hearted Brother” Scott Hylands Dead: ‘Night Heat’ & ‘Fargo’ Actor Was 83 CBS News Correspondent Nikki Battiste Joins NBC’s ‘Early Today’ As Anchor: “A True Homecoming” View All August 1, 2026 3:15pm Nikki Battiste CBS News After nearly a decade at CBS News , correspondent Nikki Battiste is taking her skills back to NBC . On Friday, the Emmy and Peabody-winning journalist announced that she’s taking on an anchor role at Early Today , in addition to contributing to Today , more than 20 years after her time as an NBC page and production associate on Today . Deadline has reached out to CBS News. “I’m thrilled to share that I will be joining NBC News as anchor of Early TODAY . I will also contribute to TODAY ,” she wrote on Instagram . “I’m honored, humbled and grateful to have the opportunity to work with the extraordinary teams at @nbc_earlytoday @todayshow and @nbcnews. Related Stories News ‘60 Minutes’ Announces New, Big-Name Correspondents & Contributors News SAG-AFTRA & WGAE Condemn CBS News’ ‘60 Minutes’ Firings, Call Terminations An Assault On Independent Journalism “This is special for me… a true homecoming. I began my journalism career as an NBC Page and then a production assistant at TODAY. NBC has always been near and dear to me. This next chapter is a dream come true.” Watch on Deadline Battiste added, “Thank you @nbc_earlytoday, @todayshow and @nbcnews – and to my family for their continued support and love. I’ll see you on the air the week of August 10th on @nbc @nbcnews and @nbcnewsnow!” View this post on Instagram NBC confirmed Battiste’s new role in an announcement on Friday, ahead of her first day on Monday and her Early Today anchoring debut on the week of Aug. 10. O’Connor, Emmy-Winning Producer and ‘The Muppet Movie’ Executive, Dies at 96 17 hours ago See All Brooke Palmer/HBO As horror fans eagerly await the next chapter in Pennywise’s (Bill Skarsgård) horrifying reign of terror, “ It: Welcome to Derry ” co-creator Andy Muschietti has shared some details on the current status of Season 2. “We’re very excited, we’re in the writers’ room right now,” Muschietti confirms to Variety . The new season will take place in 1935, centering around one of the interludes in Stephen King’s “It” novel — the Bradley Gang Massacre. As recalled in the book, a group of outlaws hides out in the town of Derry while fleeing the FBI, robbing and murdering store owners and causing all-around chaos. It takes place 27 years before the first season of “It: Welcome to Derry,” which follows the mystery surrounding a young boy gone missing amidst a Cold War military plot. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial “There’s gonna be a lot of that depression-era hustling in the air in our characters. Everybody’s trying to get by and survive the circumstances. They are gonna do crazy things,” Muschietti says. “And of course, the social, cultural, horrible things that were happening in the era, too. We’re not going to skip those. [They are the] very center and the heart of our story.” Popular on Variety While “It” fans have become accustomed to the franchise’s focus on the horror that lurks underneath images of suburban comfort and kids riding bicycles, Muschietti says Season 2’s aesthetic will differ: “In this case, on the surface, Derry is a graveyard almost. It’s a carcass of something because people are depleted, poor, tired, jobless, homeless. The kids don’t have a suburban, comforting life. They’re in a very different situation. Some of them are orphans or runaways, and so the environment is pretty bleak. But there’s always the aspect of hope that is always there, burning, and it’s what keeps our new group going.” Going back another 27 years gives Muschietti and his creative team, including co-creators Barbara Muschietti and Jason Fuchs, more of a canvas to play with; after all, the ’30s interlude in King’s original novel doesn’t take up much of the overall story. But the family bloodline will help fans connect the different timelines. “There will always be the connection, there’s a family tree that appears,” Muschietti explains. Muschietti began exploring the world of Derry and Pennywise in the 2017 hit film “It” and its 2019 sequel “It: Chapter Two.” He previously told Variety of his three-season plan for “Welcome to Derry,” exploring the time periods of 1962, 1935 and 1908, respectively, with an interest in King’s interludes: “I realized there was a hidden story there, and that Stephen King was leaving crumbs that could guide us somewhere. One that I did touch that’s not a current project, but I would love to go back to at some point is ‘The Juant,’ which is a short story that blew my mind when I read it. title: Vincent Pastore, the Mobster “Big Pussy” on ‘The Sopranos,’ Dies at 80
full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 1:47pm Vincent Pastore Michael Loccisano/Getty Images Vincent Pastore, the Bronx-born actor who portrayed Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero, the mob informant who winds up sleeping with the fishes, quite literally, on The Sopranos , has died. He was 80. Pastore was found dead by Steve Villano, the actor’s self-described “right-hand man,” in his Bronx home on Saturday, he told The Hollywood Reporte r. He apparently died in his sleep, he added. The son of a real-life wiseguy, he said, Pastore made a living running and owning bars and nightclubs for two decades and didn’t get into acting until he was 42. Yet by the time he was done, he had appeared in nearly 200 movies and TV projects — most often as an Italian American bad guy — and twice in singing roles on Broadway. Related Stories Movies Richard L. O'Connor, Emmy-Winning Producer, Dies at 96 General News Angela Wales Kirgo, Longtime Writers Guild Foundation Executive Director, Dies at 78 After landing bit parts in films including Martin Scorsese ‘s GoodFellas (1990) and Brian De Palma ‘s Carlito’s Way (1993), Pastore was impressive as the right-hand man of Alan Arkin ‘s mob boss in the comedy The Jerky Boys (1995) and as the caporegime Angelo Ruggiero opposite Armand Assante in the acclaimed 1996 HBO telefilm Gotti . Sopranos creator David Chase hired him for the role of Sal — the character wasn’t even known as Big Pussy yet — soon after he auditioned for the HBO drama in 1998. It came down to Pastore and Johnny “Roast Beef” Williams, the actor recalled in 2022 on Chazz Palminteri’s podcast . The gregarious Pastore said he “did his research” and discovered that “Big Pussy was a real guy in Jersey. He was tall and thin, out of Newark, he was friends with Frankie Valli, and there was a Little Pussy, [who] wound up being the rat in the family,” he noted. Why was the guy nicknamed Big Pussy? “Because he was a cat burglar, like Cary Grant ,” Pastore said. After Sal gets nabbed by the FBI on The Sopranos , he chooses to become an informer to avoid life in prison. He is soon sniffed out, however, and his fate is sealed when he appears to Tony ( James Gandolfini ) as a talking fish in a dream . On the second-season finale, “Funhouse,” Sal is gunned down on a boat by Tony, Paulie ( Tony Sirico ) and Silvio ( Steven Van Zandt ) and dumped overboard. Pastore, who had appeared in 21 of the show’s first 26 episodes, was extremely popular with viewers; he would show up four more times in flashbacks or dreams through the series’ 2007 conclusion. Even though he was no longer on one of TV’s hottest shows after getting whacked, he said he looked at the bright side as he was flying to Los Angeles for the first time to make a movie, Deuces Wild (2002). “I was 50 years old … and I’m on a plane and I’m going to work,” he told Palminteri. Vincent Pastore with Sopranos castmate Tony Sirico in 2012. Eric Reichbaum/Everett Collection Pastore was born in the Bronx on July 14, 1946. His father, John, was a bookmaker who had to give up that business in order to get married — the family of his future wife Natalie insisted — but resumed making loans when he retired from his job as a school custodian. The family lived in an apartment above a social club in New Rochelle, New York. After graduating from New Rochelle High School in 1964, Pastore enlisted and spent three years in the U.S. Navy and attended Pace University, where he switched his major from business to drama. But when he couldn’t find acting work, he focused on the club business around New York, starting in 1967. (He owned the Crazy Horse in New Rochelle and also drove a limo.) One night, actor brothers Matt Dillon and Kevin Dillon were at a place with him while The Pope of Greenwich Village was playing on the TV. “Matty said, ‘You could do the work that these guys are doing,’ pointing to [future Sopranos co-star] Frank Vincent and Tony Musante ,” he remembered. Pastore was hired to appear in the Sylvester Stallone -starring Gangster , directed by William Friedkin , but the project never went forward. He then made his professional acting debut in True Love (1989), starring Annabella Sciorra and Aida Turturro. Casting director Ellen Lewis saw him in that and put him in GoodFellas , and he was in Penny Marshall ‘s Awakenings in 1990, too. Pastore worked for Marshall again in Riding in Cars With Boys (2001) and with other top directors in Woody Allen’s Manhattan Murder Mystery (1993), Andrew Bergman’s It Could Happen to You (1994), Scott Kalvert’s The Basketball Diaries (1995), Sidney Lumet’s Night Falls on Manhattan (1996), Jim Abrahams ‘ Jane Austen’s Mafia! (1998), Norman Jewison ‘s The Hurricane (1999), Jon Favreau ‘s Made (2001), Guy Ritchie ‘s Revolver (2005) and Luc Besson ‘s The Family (2013). He was a leading man in the indies A Tale of Two Pizzas (2003), Heaven’s Messenger (2008), Dough Boys (2008) and Pizza With Bullets (2010) and still active recently, with a turn in the Neil Bogart biopic Spinning Gold (2023). On the small screen, Pastore sparkled in the 1997 CBS miniseries The Last Don , starring Danny Aiello , and showed up on everything from Law & Order , The Practice and Everybody Hates Chris to Blue Bloods , The Neighborhood , Gravesend and the soap operas One Life to Live and General Hospital . He participated in 2007 on Dancing with the Stars but withdrew after a week; was a contestant in 2008 on Celebrity Apprentice ; pitched a product that holds money, a “Broccoli Wad,” in 2011 on Shark Tank ; launched his own brand of tomato sauce; played in a rock band; had a podcast, Fuhgeddaboudit With Vinny Pastore ; and toured around the world with Michael Imperioli and Steve Schirripa in Talking Sopranos . Pastore did lots of stage work, and on Broadway he played Amos Hart in the 2007-08 revival of Chicago and the mob kingpin Nick Valenti in 2014 in Bullets Over Broadway . He studied acting at the HB Studios coming up and in recent years taught a workshop there. In 2014, he was diagnosed with prostate cancer. Survivors include his daughter, Renee; a sister, Sally; and a brother, Johnny. THR

He was 80. The veteran actor was found dead in his Bronx residence today, Aug. 1, by a neighbor. Pastore’s manager had not heard from him for three days though, according to a close friend, the actor’s driver had spoken to him on the phone Friday night. The death is believed to be from natural causes and is not being investigated by the medical examiner. Born in the Bronx on July 14, 1946, Pastore fought in the Vietnam war before graduating from Pace University with a degree in drama. It was David Chase’s 1999 drama The Sopranos that gave Pastore his signature role, Big Pussy, Tony Soprano’s (James Gandolfini) longtime best friend and mob enforcer turned FBI Informant whose murder became one of the Emmy-winning series’ most memorable scenes. ‘The Sopranos’ Season 1 cast, from left: Tony Sirico, Steven Van Zandt, James Gandolfini, Michael Imperioli and Vincent Pastore HBO Pastore’s extensive feature credits also include Mickey Blue Eyes, Two Family House, Riding in Cars with Boys, Witness to the Mob, Deuces Wild, Mafia!, Serving Sara, This Thing of Ours, Shark Tale, Bachelor Party Vegas, Once Upon a Time in Brooklyn, Money Train, A Brooklyn State of Mind, The Deli, Spinning Gold and Guy Ritchie’s Revolver. In TV, Pastore was a frequent guest star on Law & Order and had major roles on The Practice, Son of the Beach, Queens Supreme, Hawaii Five-0, Wu-Tang: An American Saga, the daytime drama One Life to Live and the miniseries The Last Don II . He most recently was a series regular on Gravesend and guest starred on Yellowjackets . During the 2000s, Pastore was a fixture on reality television with appearances on Celebrity Apprentice, Celebrity Family Feud, Dancing With the Stars, Shark Tank and Celebrity Fit Club . He also hosted The Wiseguy Show on SiriusXM and performed with the band The Gangster Squad. “Vinny was a great guy, he would help anyone and was very charitable,” Pastore’s longtime manager Bob McGowan said. Pastore is survived by his daughter, Renee, son-in-law and granddaughter. Nathan Congleton/NBC Savannah Guthrie shared another emotional message Saturday morning, marking six months since her mother, Nancy Guthrie , went missing, as authorities continue to search for answers in the case. Her post came after the Pima County Sheriff’s Department released two ransom notes allegedly sent by her kidnappers shortly after Nancy’s disappearance in hopes of generating new leads. Guthrie shared a photo of her mother, 84, alongside a lengthy caption, writing, “Six months ago, someone took her out of her bed in the dead of night. We have lived every moment, every breath, and every heartbeat in agony and despair ever since. Every day, we wake up and try to be strong and go on — because that’s what our joyful and resilient mom taught us to do.” Related Stories TV Sheriff in Nancy Guthrie Case Releases Ransom Notes: "She Perished Shortly After She Was Taken" TV The Reporter Who Won't Give Up on the Nancy Guthrie Kidnapping Story “But make no mistake — our hearts are in ruins. Cam and Kristine, Annie and Tommy, Mike and me — we spend every waking moment thinking of her, longing for her, looking for her,” she continued. “There is a hole inside us that can never be filled. There is an ache that cannot be softened. And there is a determination in us that cannot be quenched — to find out what happened to her, so that we can give her the dignity of a proper goodbye — a celebration of her remarkable life that she so deserves.” The Today co-anchor went on to plead for anyone with information to come forward, emphasizing that a reward remains available. “We are begging for help. We are desperate. We need someone to come forward,” she wrote. “Someone knows something. Someone suspects something. Someone recognizes the writing in the ransom demand notes. Someone has noticed something different, strange, troubling or just unusual — perhaps with someone they deeply love.” Savannah added, “Perhaps they are afraid to come forward. Perhaps they are conflicted. Perhaps they are angry or upset for being in this situation. There is a way out — to tell what you know. You can do so anonymously. The reward is available. There is a way to end this situation and do the right thing.” She concluded by asking for continued support as her family searches for answers. “We will never stop looking for answers — and we will never stop looking for the light,” she wrote. “We will always be hoping and praying and believing in the best of our world — in spite of circumstance. This is what our faith makes possible. Please. Bring her home.” Nancy was reported missing on Feb. 1 after authorities said they believed she was abducted from her home outside Tucson, Arizona. She was last seen the evening of Jan. 31. Earlier this week, the Pima County Sheriff’s Department released two ransom messages that were purportedly sent by those who kidnapped Nancy to KOLD-TV shortly after she disappeared. The first, delivered Feb. 2 and addressed to Savannah, claimed Nancy was “safe but scared” and demanded between $4 million and $6 million in Bitcoin for her release. A second note, emailed to the station’s tips line on Feb. 6, claimed the kidnappers “did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition,” adding, “She perished shortly after she was taken. The initial deadline for the first ransom demand was Feb. 5 ($4 million), while a second demand set a deadline of Feb. 9 ($6 million). title: ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary
full_text: Aug 1, 2026 12:16pm PT Critics Pick ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary Penny Lane's enchanting film turns the story of Flaco into a true-life nature fairy tale that's like the greatest children’s novel E.B. White never wrote. By Owen Gleiberman Plus Icon Owen Gleiberman Chief Film Critic @OwenGleiberman Latest ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary 14 hours ago ‘Tony’ Review: Dominic Sessa Gives His First Movie-Star Performance in Matt Johnson’s Tasty Biopic About the Young Anthony Bourdain 4 days ago ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Review: Tom Holland Returns in a ‘Mature’ but Arduous Adventure That for All Its Good Action Is Trying Too Hard 5 days ago See All David Lei “ Wild Inside ” is an enchanting movie, and a haunting one too. It’s a documentary about Flaco, the owl who escaped from the Central Park Zoo and spent a year living in the wilds of New York City. Since that story was widely covered when it happened in 2023, turning Flaco into an international media sensation, you might think: Why do I need to see a documentary about it? The answer is that Penny Lane, the gifted director of “Wild Inside,” has told this tale in a revelatory way, building it like an imagistic storybook from the ground up. From the moment that Flaco, on the evening of February 2, 2023, first appeared on a sidewalk near the corner of 50th St. and Fifth Avenue, standing there as still as a statue, he was surrounded by people filming and photographing him — civilians on their phones, then nature photographers, amateur and professional. Working with the editor Hannah Buck, Lane uses their endless archive of images to craft a true-life nature fairy tale. “Wild Inside” feels like the vérité version of the greatest children’s novel E.B. White never wrote. Related Stories 'Family Guy' Casts Kieran Culkin to Play the Devil in New Halloween Special for Hulu 'Ebenezer' Trailer: Johnny Depp Transforms Into Grouchy, Snowball-Throwing Scrooge As you watch the movie, Flaco becomes a true character , though there’s nothing cute about him, and the film has a philosophical ambiguity that takes you by surprise. It’s a movie about freedom and captivity, but it doesn’t have a simple or reductive message. Flaco, who lived in the Central Park Zoo for 13 years, escaped when someone cut the wire mesh on his cage. He was a Eurasian eagle-owl, a species that doesn’t exist in America, and when you look at him, he really is the living incarnation of the classic, mythological… owl . He’s stunningly beautiful, with big orange eyes set inside a regal head, and a body of tan and black and orange feathers that makes it appear that he’s wrapped inside the most luxurious comforter on earth. His wingspan is awesome (nearly six feet wide), but when Flaco is just standing there, which is most of the time, he does indeed look wise and inscrutable. To know what’s going on in that head, you have to read his actions. Popular on Variety The day after he made his first appearance on that midtown sidewalk, Flaco flew to Central Park and lodged himself high up in a tree near the south end of the park, just opposite the Essex House. What would happen to him? Representatives of the Central Park Zoo planned to recapture him, and they set about the task armed with mosquito nets, trying to tempt Flaco with food — the dead white lab rats he had eaten every day for 13 years. But Flaco wasn’t interested. He just stayed up in that tree. How would he survive? Tentatively, then with more confidence, he began to fly down into the park and hunt the real live New York City rats that roam there. His muscles grew stronger; his predatory instincts came to the fore. Within two weeks, he was living like a wild animal, though one who was so accustomed to being around humans that he had a way of standing on a branch as if it were his throne. The Central Park Zoo people gave up on trying to capture him. It’s only natural that the story told by “Wild Inside” triggers our liberal impulses. We think: Yes! Flaco is alive in the wild! He’s in a better place. The movie taps into what’s noble and valid and genuine about those feelings. Some of us actually have an aversion to zoos. Personally speaking, from the earliest age, I couldn’t stand them. I found staring at wild animals in captivity to be inexpressibly sad . Flaco is the animal hero who triumphs over the system of “benign” incarceration, becoming the apex predator of Central Park. And the more he thrives, and gets elevated to a kind of critter superhero status (Seth Meyers on his late-night show: “Every New Yorker dreams of moving out of their tiny shitty apartment into a nicer neighborhood. And Flaco Shawshanked out of that cage and did it!”), the more he becomes a symbol of what freedom means. After a number of months, he moves from Central Park to the East Village, and then to the Upper West Side, where we see him standing on air conditioners, and at times on elevated stone carvings in a way that’s very Batman. Residents will encounter him perched on the air conditioner just outside their apartment, staring in. From the outset, however, there are warnings in the other direction. Within a week, Flaco had triumphed over the doubters who feared that an owl raised in captivity wouldn’t have the strength or stamina to survive in the outside world. Yet it isn’t quite that simple. There have long been owls and hawks who live outside of zoos in New York, and there’s a fate that awaits them. They eat rats and mice, and in doing so they absorb the rodenticide that’s in the bodies of those creatures. Should Flaco have been recaptured and returned to his tiny environment within the Central Park Zoo? In the documentary, several knowledgable observers say that that would have been the most humane scenario — that had it happened that way, Flaco would be alive today, and would likely have lived for another 30 to 40 years. The probability of that is indisputable. What’s haunting about “Wild Inside” is that it inspires us to root for Flaco’s freedom, for the fullness of his life , in the spirit of “It’s better to burn out than to fade away.” Yet the ending that he comes to haunts us as well. He dies one day, out of the blue, by colliding into the wall of an apartment courtyard; that’s because his strength had been weakened by the rodenticide. What was the right choice? Maybe there was no right choice. “Wild Inside” is so moving because we’re stirred by the creature Flaco was, and it’s the story he lived that made him that creature. ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary Reviewed at IFC Center, New York, July 31, 2026. Executive producers: Jessica Harrop, Caitlin Mae Burke, Lisa Heller, Nancy Abraham, Tina Nguyen, Julie Parker Benello, Patty Quillin. Crew: Director: Penny Lane. Camera: Naiti Gámez. Editor: Hannah Buck. Music: Carolina Eyck. title: Netflix’s New Releases Coming in August 2026
full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 12:00pm Clockwise from top left: 'The Last House,' 'Mourinho,' 'The Whisper Man,' 'Tires,' 'MLB Field of Dreams,' 'My Brilliant Career,' 'Ricky Gervais' Alley Cats' and 'Outer Banks.' Netflix A potty-mouthed project from Ricky Gervais; Wagner Moura and Greta Lee trapped indoors; a behind-the-memes look at Jose Mourinho; a third season of Shane Gillis’ popular workplace comedy; a return to the Field of Dreams; a helping of Aussie period drama; the final chapter of OBX ; and a star-studded crime thriller top-lined by Robert De Niro are among the new film and TV highlights to hit Netflix in August. Netflix regular Ricky Gervais returns with a new project on Aug. 7, the adult animated comedy Alley Cats. The British comedian really divides opinion (some think he’s a genius talking truth-to-power and others a frightful bore who owes a lot of his reputation to the writing skills of Stephen Merchant). THR is not really making any judgements here, but we know Alley Cats will likely attract a lot of views as it features Gervais’ trademark foul-mouthed humor. The premise isn’t all that deep, its a bunch of feral alley cats swearing a lot. Each to his own. Related Stories Business Anne Sweeney Steps Down From Netflix Board Business Netflix Sued For $105 Million After Hard Drive of Unreleased Nicolas Cage Movie Was Stolen From Its Office Aug. 7 sees the release of the intriguing sci-fi thriller The Last House . Directed by French filmmaker Louis Leterrier ( Now You See Me and Fast X ) and written by Matthew Robinson ( Love and Monsters ), the film stars Greta Lee and Wagner Moura as a couple who with their two children find themselves trapped inside their house due to a looming threat and must band together to find a way out. The Special One is back on top! Jose Mourinho is about to start the new soccer season as coach of Real Madrid and just ahead of his debut at one of most famous club sides in the world we have a three-part documentary about the living legend. From the team behind Beckham , Mourinho hits Netflix on Aug. 11, and captures the remarkable story of soccer coach who has won everything there is to win in Portugal, England, Spain and Italy and also has side hustle in creating viral memes (he’s the guy behind this and the phrase, “If I speak I am in big trouble.”). The doc features interviews with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson, John Terry, Iker Casillas, Zlatan Ibrahimović, Didier Drogba, Marcelo, Samuel Eto’o, Javier Zanetti, Frank Lampard, Petr Čech and more. Comedian Shane Gillis’ time in the spotlight continues apace with the much-anticipated release of the third season of his series Tires on Aug. 13. The workplace comedy, that unsurprisingly takes place in a struggling Pennsylvanian tire shop, isn’t overly complex but is undoubtedly one of the funniest things on Netflix at the moment. Gillis and co-creators Steve Gerben, John McKeever have put together a great cast of oddball characters, including Stavros Halkias’ Dave and Thomas Haden Church’s Phil Jacobs. Other recurring performers include Andrew Schulz and Matt McCusker. The critics weren’t impressed but the audience loved it. If you don’t think too hard about it, you’ll have a great time. Also on Aug. 13, we have Netflix’s big live sports event of the month, the MLB Field of Dreams 2026. If you’re unfamiliar with the special game, the MLB plays a regular season game in a ballpark adjacent to Field of Dreams in Dyersville, Iowa. Yes that Field of Dreams , from the 1989 film starring Kevin Costner. It’s a bit gimmicky but fun nonetheless. This year the Minnesota Twins take on the Philadelphia Phillies. It’s all happening on Aug. 13, as we have another pick, this time our international pick of the month, the Australian series, My Brilliant Career. Some people maybe familiar with the Miles Franklin novel, others with Gillian Armstrong’s 1979 film adaptation starring Judy Davis and the late Sam Neill, which has become something of an urtext for Australian New Wave cinema and feminist cinema. This new six-episode adaptation, developed by Liz Doran, stars Philippa Northeast as the Sybylla Melvyn, a precocious 17-year-old living in rural Australia in 1900 who wants to become a writer. Alas her plans are disrupted by romance with Harry (Christopher Chung). On Aug. 20th, the Outer Banks saga comes to a likely epic conclusion, with the launch of the fifth and final season of the popular action/mystery teen drama. OBX , as the kids call it, has been something of a star factory for Netflix, producing the likes of rising stars Chase Stokes, Madelyn Cline, Madison Bailey, Jonathan Daviss and more, and the cast are back for one more run around with the final season in which the Pogues find themselves stranded in Morocco still mourning the death of one of their best friends and still trying to win their freedom. At the end of August, on the 28th to be precise, Netflix releases its most starry original feature film, James Ashcroft’s The Whisper Man. The crime thriller is based on Alex North’s bestselling book, and tells the story of a widowed crime writer looking for his abducted son, and asks for help from his estranged father, who also happens to be a retired former police detective. Together they “discover a connection to decades-old case of a convicted serial killer known as “The Whisper Man.”” The cast is genuinely the biggest draw for this project as it includes Robert De Niro, Michelle Monaghan, Adam Scott, Michael Keaton, John Carroll Lynch, Hamish Linklater, and Owen Teague. The film was written by Ben Jacoby and Chase Palmer. Movies added to Netflix in August include About Last Night…, Anaconda, Annie, Are We Done Yet?, Bride of Chucky, Cult of Chucky, Curse of Chucky, Seed of Chucky, Child’s Play 2, Child’s Play 3, Clueless, Daddy Day Camp, Daddy Day Care, Elysium, The Fast and the Furious, 2 Fast 2 Furious, The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift, Fast Five, Fast & Furious, Fast & Furious 6, Furious 7, Field of Dreams, The Hitman’s Bodyguard, The Hitman’s Wife’s Bodyguard, Holmes & Watson, Marie Antoinette, Mile 22, Minions, National Security, Nightcrawler, Party Girl, Selma, Something’s Gotta Give, Speed, Speed 2: Cruise Control, Tears of the Sun, The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones, Zero Dark Thirty, Swiss Army Man, M3GAN, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo, The Shallows, Smurfs: The Lost Village, Eighth Grade, Five Nights at Freddy’s 2, Sing and Ingrid Goes West. Today, we mourn not only Nims, but every life lost in this tragedy.” The statement, posted on Instagram – read it in its entirety below – continued, “The world has lost one of mountaineering’s greatest climbers, a leader who inspired millions through his courage, humility and unwavering belief that human potential is far greater than we often imagine.” Watch on Deadline Purja’s brother Kamal later said in a statement, “It is with the heaviest heart that I share the devastating news that my beloved younger brother, Nirmal ‘Nimsdai’ Purja, and the other climbers are no longer with us. Purja, who lived in Hampshire, England, is survived by his wife and and three-year-old daughter. Complete information on survivors was not immediately available.
